verdict.line: You lose if you let the lane drag past level 6 and Nasus stacks Siphoning Strike unchecked; you win if you convert your early dash-and-hook pressure into kills before his ultimate comes online.

brief.thesis: Kled's power is front-loaded into levels 1-5 through Jousting resets and Bear Trap yanks, while Nasus's power is backloaded into infinite Siphoning Strike stacks and a level-6 Fury of the Sands spike. The 50.7% win rate over 75 games and Kled's lane/solo-kill advantage both exist because he's supposed to win the fight before stacks and ult exist, not after. Every decision in this lane is a race against Nasus's clock.

theirWindow.when: Level 6, Fury of the Sands up
theirWindow.what: Nasus gains bonus health, range, and max-health drain damage while the storm rages. Do not commit to an extended trade or dive the moment he hits 6 — bait the ult off cooldown first or disengage.

yourWindow.what: Use E (Jousting) to dash in, then recast to dash back through him, chaining into Q (Bear Trap on a Rope) to hook and yank him into extra trade time. His Q (Siphoning Strike) only hits one target at 255 range with no slow, so he can't punish your dash windows the way you can punish his.

start.why: 85.1% pick rate at 45% win rate over 80 games — the sustain and AD let you trade through his Q (Siphoning Strike) pokes without losing the race to level 6.

boots.why: 66.7% pick, 50% win rate over 58 games — flat reduction on Siphoning Strike and his auto-attacks matters more than tenacity since Wither is his only CC.

core.why: First item in the most popular path (50% WR, 18.2% pick) — the max-health scaling AoE proc lets you threaten through his growing health pool.
Second in the 50%-WR, 18.2%-pick path — armor shred compounds with Jousting's physical damage during your pre-6 all-in window.
Completes the top core path at 50% win rate over 10 games — sustain and damage to keep winning extended trades once stacks start evening the fight.

runes.keystoneWhy: Stacking adaptive force and healing rewards the repeated Jousting-and-Bear-Trap engagements you need to force before level 6, and keeps you ahead in the sustain race against his Soul Eater lifesteal.

summoners.why: 84.4% pick rate at 46.9% win rate — Ignite denies the Soul Eater lifesteal heal exactly when you're trying to close out a pre-6 kill, and Flash secures the follow-through on a Bear Trap yank.

playing.title: Front-load your aggression
playing.detail: Chain E (Jousting) with its recast into Q (Bear Trap on a Rope) to force extended trades at levels 1-5, before his Siphoning Strike stacks or Wither rank make the fight even.

playing.title: Count his Q stacks
playing.detail: Watch how often Nasus lands the killing blow with Siphoning Strike on casters and cannon minions. High stacks mean his sustain and damage are catching up to your early edge.

playing.title: Trade through Wither, don't dodge it
playing.detail: Wither decelerates both your movement and attack speed over time rather than stunning, so burning E (Jousting) to flee wastes a dash. Pop W (Violent Tendencies) and fight through the slow instead.

playing.title: All-in before level 6
playing.detail: OP.GG's own read on this matchup is to pressure early and respect level 6. Once Fury of the Sands is up, he gains health, range, and max-health drain — disengage from extended fights until you bait the ult down.

playing.title: Use Pocket Pistol if dismounted
playing.detail: If Skaarl dies mid-trade, your Q becomes Pocket Pistol — a ranged knockback that buys space to rebuild courage before remounting and re-engaging.

playing.title: Step off Spirit Fire
playing.detail: E (Spirit Fire) reduces the armor of anyone standing in it. Don't anchor extended trades inside the zone or his autos and Siphoning Strike start hitting harder than they should.

brief.patchCaveat: Build paths, runes, summoners, and all win-rate/sample numbers above are measured from real games on the current patch via OP.GG; the power-curve timing and trade reasoning are our own tactical read on the recorded ability kit.

stats.opponentTip: Apply pressure during early game to gain control over lane. Be careful of being killed when Nasus reaches level 6.
